unsupportedClaims: 'the navigation dropped "What is RI?" entirely' — the evidence lists nav items added and removed, but 'What is RI?' does not appear in the navRemoved list; it is not confirmed in the evidence

'Gong built an entire product category around "Revenue Intelligence" — then quietly removed it from the top of its own homepage' — 'quietly' implies deliberate concealment; no evidence supports this framing

'Gong built its early identity around a category it invented' — 'a category it largely invented' / 'it invented' is not supported by the evidence; the evidence describes category-definition language and '#1 revenue intelligence platform' but does not confirm Gong invented the category

'reportedly led to declines in net dollar retention' — the evidence says 'pressured Gong's per-seat pricing model and led to declines in net dollar retention'; the article strips 'reportedly' and presents this as confirmed fact in the business context section

'reaching a reported $7.25 billion valuation by mid-2021' — the evidence cites this valuation for the Series E; the article states it without the sourcing qualifier 'reportedly' in the body text, presenting it as a direct fact rather than a reported figure

'This may suggest the page is now written for buying committees' — the 'may suggest' hedge is present but the causal chain (removing named VPs → targeting committees) is not conditioned on any supporting evidence

'This swap — from named people to named actions — suggests the page may now be built for someone who wants to evaluate on their own terms before talking to anyone' — intent attribution presented as a pattern inference without a stated condition
'a nav rebuilt for visitors who arrive knowing what Gong is' — inferred cause; no evidence confirms visitor awareness levels at the time of nav changes

'the gap between the claim and the demo creates credibility damage' — conversion outcome inference not supported by any data in the evidence

Add 'reportedly' or equivalent hedging every time a specific dollar figure (Series D $200M, Series E $250M, $7.25B valuation) appears in the body text to match the evidence's own sourcing qualifiers

Rewrite the opening paragraph to remove 'That is not a rebrand' — the evidence does not confirm whether Gong classified this as a rebrand or not; replace with a conditioned inference such as 'Whether or not Gong called it a rebrand internally, the copy changes suggest...'

Remove or condition the claim that Gong 'invented' or 'largely invented' the revenue intelligence category — the evidence does not support this; replace with 'helped define' or 'was the category leader in'

In the CTA section, remove the implicit underperformance framing for named-VP CTAs — the evidence shows they were removed but provides no click or conversion data to support any performance inference; rephrase as a structural observation only

Add the condition 'if Gong's inbound traffic profile shifted toward branded or comparison-intent queries' to the claim about the page being written for visitors who 'already know what Gong is' — currently presented without this condition as required by the evidence review

The phrase 'bottom-of-funnel actions, meaning steps a buyer takes when they are close to a decision' is a good plain-language explanation — apply the same pattern earlier in the article where CRO terms like 'buying committees' are introduced without definition
The repetition of 'the page may now be written for...' across three separate sections weakens impact; consolidate this observation into one section and vary the framing elsewhere
